text: **dsh-next-hint**（DSH 网页插件）：在一轮对话结束后，为空闲的 composer 提供一条可采纳的下一步提示。浏览器端在会话停止且草稿为空时请求主机端；主机读取最近会话消息，经当前会话路由或配置的模型生成简短建议，再以输入框中的幽灵文字显示。用户可按 Tab 将建议插入草稿，开始输入或切换会话时提示会消失。适合希望顺着当前编码任务继续推进、又想自行决定发送内容的 DSH 网页用户。配置项均有默认值，不要求额外密钥；辅助模型请求使用当前 DSH 模型路由。

**dsh-next-hint** (DSH web plugin) suggests a next prompt after a turn settles. It uses recent session messages to show ghost text in an empty composer. Tab inserts it into the draft; typing or switching sessions clears it. Settings have defaults; generation follows the current DSH model route.
想在一轮对话结束后自动看到下一句可以怎么问。
能不能根据当前会话内容给我一个后续提示词？
Show me a contextual follow-up prompt in the composer after each completed turn.
**dsh-next-hint** 的功能「会话后续提示」：一轮结束且草稿为空时，根据最近会话消息生成一条短建议，并以输入框幽灵文字呈现；按 Tab 插入草稿，不会替用户发送。
**dsh-next-hint** 的功能「提示采纳与清除」：在输入框聚焦且没有候选菜单占用 Tab 时，按 Tab 将提示写入草稿；用户开始输入、切换会话或组件卸载时会清除提示。
dsh-next-hint 会将最近会话消息整理成上下文，并通过 DSH 当前模型路由发起辅助生成请求；所用服务取决于该路由或配置的 provider/model。
dsh-next-hint 的维护与更新元数据：活跃维护；距最后推送 17 天；提交数 15；更新频次 unknown；近 90 天提交 未知；开放 Issue 未知；仓库健康分 62/100（置信度 low）。

dsh-next-hint README · dsh-next-hint：> When a turn ends, the composer suggests the next message by itself.
> **Tab accepts, nothing is ever sent.**

A [DeepSeek Harness](https://www.deepseek.com/harness/) plugin that brings
Claude Code–style prompt suggestions to DSH — as **ghost text** inside your own
composer: visible, undoable, and never on the return key.

dsh-next-hint README · dsh-next-hint：```text
┌────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
│ fix the two failing cases as well              Tab accept   │  ← ghost, appears on settle
└────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘
                     ↑ only while the draft is empty; typing dismisses it

dsh-next-hint README · Why install it：- **It knows what you were doing.** One **decoupled auxiliary request** reads the
  last few turns of *this* session — the file you touched, the test that went red,
  where the work stopped — instead of a template like "continue?".
- **It never touches your Enter key.** Accepting inserts ordinary text into the
  draft. `Ctrl+Z` undoes it; sending stays your decision. There is no send path in
  the code at all.
- **It stays quiet.** No route, timeout, rate limit, malformed output, or a plain
  "not today" all end as **no ghost** and no error surface — at most one warn in
  the log.
- **It does not ship your conversation anywhere.** The browser posts a
  `sessionId`; the host reads the transcript inside its own process, writes it
  nowhere, logs no text, and keeps it on this machine.

dsh-next-hint README · Install：**DSH Desktop**: Settings → Plugins → add a git package

```text
github:xiaoshenming/dsh-next-hint#main
```

The desktop profile is owned by the app — `dsh plugin --profile desktop …` is refused by the CLI.
For a self-managed profile such as `web`:

```bash
dsh plugin --profile web add "github:xiaoshenming/dsh-next-hint#main"
```

Restart the app once — plugins join the roster at boot.

dsh-next-hint README · Install：> **Updating:** the plugin page's update check only compares npm-registry sources; a
> `github:` install is skipped and always reads as "latest". For a GitHub install use
> one of these, then restart the app:
>
> ```bash
> cd ~/.dsh/profiles/desktop && pnpm update dsh-next-hint
> ```
>
> or uninstall it on the plugin page and add `github:xiaoshenming/dsh-next-hint#main`
> again. To use the in-app update button, install the plugin from npm once it is published.

dsh-next-hint README · What you get：| Moment | What happens |
| --- | --- |
| A turn settles, draft is empty | One grey line at the composer's first line, `Tab accept` on the right |
| `Tab` with focus in the composer | The sentence lands in the draft, caret at its end, **not sent** |
| You start typing | The ghost disappears |
| You switch sessions | The ghost is dropped |
| Two declines / timeout / no route | Nothing at all — the correct outcome |

dsh-next-hint README · What you get：A model that answers "nothing to suggest" is asked once more with a stricter
instruction before the plugin gives up: one refusal never blanks the whole turn.

Tab only fires when no candidate menu owns it: with the `/` or `@` menu open,
Tab still belongs to the menu.
dsh-next-hint README · Configuration：Settings → Plugins → dsh-next-hint. Every key has a default; nothing is required.

dsh-next-hint README · Configuration：| Key | Default | Meaning |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `enabled` | `true` | Master switch |
| `provider` / `model` | empty | Empty follows the session's last route; set both or neither |
| `locale` | `auto` | Language of the suggestion |
| `maxTurns` | `3` | Exchanges sampled |
| `maxInputBytes` | `8000` | Input budget for the auxiliary request |
| `maxOutputTokens` | `128` | Output token cap |
| `maxHintChars` | `48` | Hint length cap; a paragraph is dropped, a long sentence truncated |
| `timeoutMs` | `15000` | Per-call timeout |
| `perSessionCooldownMs` | `0` | Per-session cooldown; default suggests every turn |

dsh-next-hint README · How it works：A dual-face cordis plugin, the same shape as
[dsh-session-surgeon](https://github.com/xiaoshenming/dsh-session-surgeon):

```text
browser   session.running true → false, draft empty
            └─ POST /api/next-hint  { sessionId }        ← id only, no transcript
host      loopback + origin check → single flight + cooldown
            └─ ctx.sessions.get(id).deriveMessages()      ← recent turns

Deliberate choices:

dsh-next-hint README · How it works：- **Decide in the browser, generate in the host.** Only the browser knows whether
  the draft is empty, whether you are typing, and which session is on screen;
  asking the host to guess gets it wrong twice.
- **One request/response.** No SSE, no long-lived connections, no server-side
  cache. Cancelling is `AbortController.abort()`.
- **Official slot, own pixels.** The component mounts in
  `conversation.composer.dock`; the ghost node is ours because the host exposes
  no inline-hint write path. Unmounting removes the node, the listeners, and the
  in-flight request.
- **The auxiliary call follows the session-title recipe**: its own system
  instruction, its own timeout, the cheapest reasoning level, and a failure that
  cannot touch the main conversation.
dsh-next-hint README · Related work：Four same-kind plugins now exist, plus one complementary tool; **prefer one same-kind**:

dsh-next-hint README · Related work：- **This plugin**: official dock slot and a stateless host route; Tab accepts, the offer is
  dropped on a session switch.
- [Composer predictions (`dsh-composer-prediction`)](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness/discussions/10053):
  same idea; overlay slot, per-session cache, Esc, settings page. From 0.7.7 it detects this
  plugin and pauses itself (this plugin wins).
- [Composer Predictions (`dsh-composer-predictions`)](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness/discussions/10769):
  same idea plus draft continuation; Alt+↑/↓ candidate cycling, Esc, owner admission; needs
  DSH ≥0.2.1-rc.3.
- [Reply Suggestions (`dsh-reply-suggestions`)](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness/discussions/9656):
  same idea; Enter-to-fill, Esc, usage/cost stats; built for rc.2.
- **Complementary**: [`dsh-input-assist`](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness/discussions/6313)
  completes *the sentence you are typing* and checks typos; this plugin suggests *the next
  message after a turn*. The only overlap is an idle empty composer — if you see two ghosts
  there, turn one of them off.

dsh-next-hint README · Compatibility：- Measured on **DSH Desktop `0.2.1-rc.2` (Windows)** and the same version's **web profile (macOS)**. The host half needs
  `ctx.llm`, `ctx.sessions`, and `ctx.webServer.register`; the browser half needs
  the `conversation.composer.dock` slot and the composer input facade.
- Still `0.x`: if upstream moves those seams, the ghost breaks first. Its position
  relies on the editor's `[data-input-scroll]` structure; a missing anchor means
  no ghost, silently.
- Requests from outside loopback are refused by the route.
- If DSH ships this natively, this plugin can be disabled cleanly — nothing here
  assumes it is the only writer of the composer.
